**Grant Application: Glocks and Fried Chicken (GAFC) to Everytown Safety Fund**

Glocks and Fried Chicken (GAFC), a minority-owned social enterprise, requests **$150,000** from the Everytown Safety Fund to expand vital gun safety education within Sacramento's communities of color.

Sacramento's communities of color face alarmingly disproportionate rates of gun violence, including accidental shootings, suicides, and interpersonal violence. This crisis demands culturally relevant, proactive intervention, particularly for youth and families who often lack access to comprehensive safety resources.

GAFC offers a multi-faceted approach. Our innovative "Gloxsie 21" cartoon IP educates children on foundational gun safety principles in an engaging format. Concurrently, our AI education program empowers youth with crucial technological skills alongside responsible gun ownership information, bridging the digital divide while fostering safety. Complementing this, our robust community workshops, partnered with the respected Church of Legacy, provide hands-on safety training and open dialogue for adults and families.

With your support, GAFC will significantly reduce accidental firearm injuries, promote safe storage practices, and foster a generation equipped with both gun safety knowledge and valuable tech skills. Our goal is tangible decreases in gun-related incidents and increased community resilience.

As a minority-owned social enterprise rooted deeply in the communities we serve, GAFC brings authentic understanding and trust often missing from traditional programs. Our unique, engaging methodologies, coupled with our strategic partnership, position us uniquely to drive impactful, sustainable change. An investment of $150,000 from Everytown will directly translate into safer homes and empowered lives across Sacramento, creating a model for community-led gun violence prevention.
